Local Government / Public Sector.AU-01: Run an introductory AI awareness session for staff and leaders explaining what AI is, how it works, and where it is already being used in government and public services.
Local Government / Public Sector.AU-02: Hold a short workshop with key teams to identify where AI could help reduce manual work, improve decision-making, or strengthen outcomes in government and public services.
Local Government / Public Sector.AU-03: Create a simple myth-vs-fact guide that clarifies what AI can and cannot do in government and public services, avoiding hype and fear.
Local Government / Public Sector.AU-04: Offer optional AI learning or demonstration sessions where staff can safely explore basic tools and ask questions.
Local Government / Public Sector.AU-05: Facilitate a discussion about how AI may change day-to-day tasks in government and public services, emphasising that it is there to support, not replace, people.
Local Government / Public Sector.LV-01: Include AI as a regular topic in leadership or governance meetings to explore how it could support strategic goals in government and public services.
Local Government / Public Sector.LV-02: Approve one small, low-risk AI pilot so the organisation can gain hands-on experience and learn from a controlled experiment.
Local Government / Public Sector.LV-03: Work with leaders to map AI opportunities to core organisational priorities such as service quality, efficiency, or stakeholder outcomes in government and public services.
Local Government / Public Sector.LV-04: Set aside regular time for leaders to review examples of how similar organisations in government and public services are using AI safely and effectively.
Local Government / Public Sector.LV-05: Create a simple evaluation checklist for AI tools that covers privacy, security, accuracy, usability, and risk considerations relevant to government and public services.
Local Government / Public Sector.DR-01: Document your main data sources—such as records, logs, transactions, or case information—so staff clearly understand what information exists in government and public services.
Local Government / Public Sector.DR-02: Select one important dataset used for decisions in government and public services and review it for accuracy, completeness, and timeliness.
Local Government / Public Sector.DR-03: Check whether authorised staff can access the information they need for routine decisions in government and public services without unnecessary delays or bottlenecks.
Local Government / Public Sector.DR-04: Review who has access to sensitive or critical data in government and public services and tighten permissions where needed to prevent accidental misuse.
Local Government / Public Sector.DR-05: Ask IT or system owners to confirm whether your current systems can support basic AI-assisted tools—such as summarisation or reporting—without creating undue risk in government and public services.
Local Government / Public Sector.PS-01: Provide refresher training to strengthen staff confidence with the core digital tools they use in government and public services before introducing AI-enabled features.
Local Government / Public Sector.PS-02: Encourage staff to try a safe, low-risk AI-assisted tool—such as summarising text or generating simple drafts—and share what helped their work in government and public services.
Local Government / Public Sector.PS-03: Give managers a short guide on how to support staff adopting new technology, including how to answer basic AI questions and address concerns in government and public services.
Local Government / Public Sector.PS-04: Share a curated set of beginner-friendly AI learning resources tailored to common roles and tasks in government and public services.
Local Government / Public Sector.PS-05: Clearly explain how AI can reduce repetitive or low-value work in government and public services, allowing people to focus on higher-value, human-centred tasks.
Local Government / Public Sector.GT-01: Send a reminder about privacy and data-handling expectations, including examples of what information from government and public services must never be entered into AI tools.
Local Government / Public Sector.GT-02: Develop a simple, plain-English ‘responsible use of AI’ guideline that outlines safe, ethical, and compliant behaviours for staff in government and public services.
Local Government / Public Sector.GT-03: Share a brief internal update explaining which AI tools or pilots are being explored, why they were chosen, and how they support work in government and public services.
Local Government / Public Sector.GT-04: Introduce a basic AI risk-check process that teams must complete before trialling new tools, prompting them to consider accuracy, privacy, fairness, and operational impact in government and public services.
Local Government / Public Sector.GT-05: Create a lightweight approval pathway for AI pilots that ensures oversight from relevant leaders (e.g., governance, risk, IT) before tools are used more broadly in government and public services.
